summary:
Space Debris Visualizer: project summary

This project converts a JavaScript web app for exploring orbital debris into a standalone Python desktop application built with Tkinter, NumPy and Matplotlib.

Features
- Four tabs: Overview, History, Statistics and AI Search, plus a dark/light theme toggle.
- A rotating 3D globe showing debris coloured by risk. You can drag it, and objects hidden behind Earth aren't drawn.
- Charts for orbit type, size distribution, growth over time and risk by orbit.
- Filters for orbit, size, year, risk and country, applied instantly.

AI search agent
The original agent gave wrong answers because of word-matching bugs and unit mix-ups. The new one parses plain-English questions into exact filters. It handles counts, averages, rankings, breakdowns, ID lookups and combined queries such as "Russian debris larger than 50 cm since 2019 in LEO". It shows how it understood each question. Its answers matched brute-force checks in all 36 tests, and each query takes about 0.16ms.

Files
`debris_data.py` (data), `debris_ai.py` (AI), `debris_charts.py` (charts and globe), `space_debris_app.py` (GUI), plus tests and `requirements.txt`.

Limitation
The data is still randomly generated mock data. I couldn't open the real window here, so the visual layout is untested.
